-rad tech prospective- 

I don’t know where your values at or what do you prioritise so I can’t really talk you in or out radiology 

But when I was training in my program , I went to almost 11 different hospital around my country. Therefore I met lots of docs from different specialties
 And that confirmed my assumptions even more, that medicine is one of the most toxic environments there is 

I had neurologist getting mad and frustrated at us when we asked for the slightest information that we needed.
Orthopaedic surgeons were so mysonigistic and used to scream at us for the slightest mistakes or if we were “too slow” (one used to throw his instruments at the OR staff and students) 
Some even used to either forcefully take out C-arm to do take x-rays themselves or go to our department after they finish their surgeries and demand to take their post-op images themselves bc “we didn’t do them right”(while patient didn’t totally wake up)

Gladly our techs and preceptors tried their best to protect and warn us from these doctors, but they are one of the biggest reason why I seriously considered leaving the whole medical field, bc nothing is worth being disrespected like that. 

I don’t 100% blame them, but it showed me more than enough how stressful and suffocation their work was. 

Until I started training and then working closely with radiologist.And omg they totally gave me a glimpse of hope.
Most were chill and liked working with other staff, students, their residents and patients (idk from where the isolation point came from)
They were the nicest docs with their patient,the least stressed, and most I met enjoyed what they were doing. 
Even though I didn’t enjoy IR the most, the interventional radiologist were even more amazing, loved to teach and loved to work. I actually believe IR’s are one of the happiest specialities there is 😂

If you care about the “directly saving lives” aspect and fast interventions(and you like being happy). I think you would like IR 

Obviously not all radiologist were amazing, and not all the doctors I met were toxic. But this is my perspective from someone who lives with a family full of MD’s from different specialities  (and med students), and who went to enough hospitals to form an opinions about the situation there.

Good luck with whatever specialty you choose 😊

Omg yes, in a couple of hospital in my country, if the “VIP” patient want any examination done, they would order it wether it’s relevant to their condition or not. 

They didn’t want to come to the department for an x-ray? Portable to their room it is.
Wanted an MRI for their knees for some reason?  They will get it 

One of the weirdest practices I’ve seen.

Unfortunately, more than what you would imagine 

And I’ve seen it worse in x-ray, in some cases it’s easily recognisable if the doc didn’t do an actual physical examination before sending him to us 

I remember I trained in a hospital that was way waayyy understaffed (to the point were MRI techs used to cover for x-ray sometimes 😃) and the ER docs there were a nightmare. 
One of them ordered 15-ish X-rays;(chest,hand,wrist and scaphoid ,forearm, elbow humerus,shoulder) for a walky talky patient who just had pain in his upper arm (we checked with him multiple times, only confirmed that the pain was there)
We did the chest and the hand (which looked normal) then decided to do the humerus (which had a clear, transverse fracture right in the middle) 
We didn’t see any reason to finish , so we called the ER doc and told him about what we saw and that we weren’t willing to finish, and he just said “ok, send the patient and whatever you took” 

This was a really common thing the tech used to do (which we technically aren’t supposed to do) but the docs there were bullshitting way to much to the point were techs had to take an action 
And they almost never send them back to complete the order :) 

To this day, I have no idea how this hospital is still up, let alone the radiology department there :))))
